name: Amy Canham
letter:
Amy Canham is the kind of person who makes you feel like the most important person in the room the moment you walk in. I've watched her do this over and over — not as a performance, but as a reflex. She genuinely sees people. In a world that moves fast and rewards the loudest voices, Amy slows down. She asks the question nobody else thought to ask. She remembers the thing you mentioned in passing three months ago. That's not a skill. That's a character.

I don't know if Amy realizes what she gives people just by being present. But I do. And I wanted to write it down before another day passed without saying it.

name: Erik Severinghaus
letter:
Erik Severinghaus built something from nothing and made it look easy — which is how you know it wasn't. The kind of person who could have coasted on talent alone but chose discipline instead. I've seen a lot of people with big ideas and small follow-through. Erik is the opposite. He's quiet about what he's working on until it's done, and then it's done well.

What I respect most is that he hasn't let success make him smaller — hasn't made him someone who forgets where he started or who helped him get there. That's rarer than people think.

name: Ben Dickey
letter:
Ben Dickey is one of those people who carries something heavy with grace. You wouldn't know it if you didn't know him — he leads with humor, with warmth, with the kind of laugh that fills a room. But underneath that is a man who has done real work on himself. Who has chosen, deliberately, who he wants to be.

I think about Ben when I need to be reminded that strength doesn't have to be loud. That showing up consistently, being honest, being kind — that's the work. He does the work.

name: Amera M.
letter:
Amera moves through the world with a kind of clarity I find rare. She knows what she believes and why she believes it — not because she was told, but because she asked hard questions and sat with hard answers. That kind of integrity is quiet. It doesn't announce itself. But you feel it.

She's someone who makes you want to be more honest. Not because she pressures you to be, but because being around her, dishonesty feels like a waste of everyone's time. I mean that as the highest compliment I know how to give.

name: Aaron Huppert
letter:
Aaron Huppert is the kind of friend who shows up. Not just when it's convenient — when it costs something. I've seen him drive across town for someone who needed help moving. Sit on the phone for an hour when someone needed to be heard. Give time he didn't have because someone else needed it more.

That's not a small thing. In a culture that celebrates hustle and busyness as virtue, Aaron quietly practices something harder: availability. Generosity. Presence. I don't think he'd call it anything. He'd just say he was being a friend. That's exactly what makes it worth writing down.
